reviewers.summary: The change addresses the prior bypass by counting indirect variable and module principals, but the new conservative rule also counts grants to unrelated identities and can reject a valid configuration.

findingList.message: The contract test treats every variable or module principal as the app identity. Resolve those references or exclude principals that cannot be shown to identify the app, so valid ACR grants to unrelated identities do not fail the exact-one assertion.

evidence.codePathTraced: MayResolveToApp returns true for every var or module principal reference without resolving whether it identifies the app identity. AppAcrGrantRoles then includes that assignment in the exact-role assertion.
evidence.failureScenario: If an unrelated identity receives AcrPull on the ACR through var.reader_principal_id or module.reader.principal_id, the contract test counts it as an app grant and fails, even though the app identity still has exactly one ACR grant.

reviewers.summary: The change addresses the prior bypass by counting indirect principals, but it now treats every variable or module principal as the app identity. That makes the contract test reject valid ACR grants to unrelated identities.

findingList.message: The contract test misclassifies unresolved variable and module principals as app grants. Resolve these references or distinguish them from grants to the app identity so valid ACR grants to other identities do not fail AC RELEASE-ID-01.

evidence.codePathTraced: MayResolveToApp returns true for every var.* or module.* principal reference without resolving whether it identifies the app identity. AppAcrGrantRoles then includes that assignment in the app grant list.
evidence.failureScenario: If an unrelated identity receives AcrPush on the ACR through var.reader_principal_id or module.worker.principal_id, the test counts it as an app grant and fails the exact-one AcrPull assertion, even though the app identity still has only its required AcrPull grant.
